newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs, franc seen firm next week.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs, franc seen firm next week.

text.p: Linear bond (OLO) futures set an all-time high on Friday after U.S. jobs data, which sparked a full-point jump in U.S. bond futures.

The front-month contract was up 34 basis points at 122.59 BGBc1 at 1528 GMT, above the 122.22 close of December 3, 1996, which marked the previous high. French bond futures also set a contract high. The cash benchmark 2007 OLO yielded 5.69 percent, down from 5.75 Thursday.
Dealers expected the firm trend to continue next week. "There are few key economic data expected which could change the course of the market," Kredietbank's Conrad Fieremans said.

Money market dealers said they expected the franc to firm next week. Money yields would ease to levels from just before the Dassault bribery scandal broke at the end of January, sparking unrest over the ruling coalition's future.

One-week repo yields, which rose to as high as 3.15 percent last week, eased to 3.06/09 percent. "Yields should ease further to just above three percent," one money broker said. He added Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse was right when he called the franc weakness "ridiculous" in a newspaper.
"When we move to 20.69 to the mark, the central bank gets nervous. Not at these levels," he said.
The franc was at 20.6295/05 to the mark at 1550 GMT, recovering from above 20.63 seen early this week.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
